User.title: User
User.description: Represents a registered user within the LinkFlow application. This entity stores basic user information, excluding sensitive authentication credentials like passwords, which are managed by an external authentication system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

email.description: The user's email address, used for identification and login.

name.description: The display name of the user.

isAdmin.description: A flag indicating if the user has administrator privileges.

createdAt.description: Unix timestamp indicating when the user account was created.

updatedAt.description: Unix timestamp indicating when the user account was last updated.

Tag.title: Tag
Tag.description: Represents a category or keyword used to organize learning links. Tags provide a flexible way to filter and group related content.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Tag entity.

createdAt.description: Unix timestamp indicating when the tag was created.

updatedAt.description: Unix timestamp indicating when the tag was last updated.

LearningLink.title: LearningLink
LearningLink.description: Represents a single learning resource (e.g., article, video, tutorial) managed by a user in the LinkFlow application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the LearningLink entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who owns this learning link. (Relationship: User 1:N LearningLink)

title.description: The title of the learning link.

url.description: The URL of the learning resource.

description.description: An optional summary or description of the learning resource, potentially AI-generated.

tagIds.description: References to Tags associated with this learning link. (Relationship: Tag N:N LearningLink)

isCompleted.description: A flag indicating whether the user has completed or 'taken' this learning link.

color.description: The visual color scheme for the link card. Possible values: 'emerald', 'blue', 'amber', 'rose', 'slate'.

icon.description: The icon representing the type of learning link. Possible values: 'Book', 'Video', 'Globe', 'Code', 'Image', 'Audio', 'File', 'Chat'.

createdAt.description: Unix timestamp indicating when the learning link was created.

updatedAt.description: Unix timestamp indicating when the learning link was last updated.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, corresponding to `request.auth.uid`.

definition.description: A dedicated collection for granting administrator privileges. The mere existence of a document for a `userId` here signifies admin status, ensuring Authorization Independence (no `get()` calls to user profiles for role checks).

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who has administrator privileges.

definition.description: A global collection for managing shared tags that can be applied to LearningLinks. These tags are accessible across all users for filtering and organization.

params.name: tagId
params.description: The unique identifier for the tag.

definition.description: Stores individual learning links, privately owned by a specific user. Includes denormalized `userId` for Authorization Independence, enabling direct ownership checks without `get()` calls to parent documents.

params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this learning link.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed following the core principles of Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and Access Modeling, ensuring a secure, scalable, and debuggable system for LinkFlow. We've established distinct collections for users, their private learning links, global tags, and administrator roles.

**Authorization Independence:**
1.  **Learning Links:** Each `LearningLink` document stored at `/users/{userId}/learningLinks/{learningLinkId}` explicitly includes a `userId` field matching the parent `userId` in the path. This denormalization is crucial. When evaluating security rules for a `LearningLink`, we can directly compare `request.auth.uid` with `resource.data.userId` and the `{userId}` wildcard in the path. This eliminates the need for expensive and complex `get()` calls to the parent `User` document, allowing for atomic operations and simplifying rule logic significantly. For instance, creating a new learning link for a user doesn't require checking the parent `User` document's existence in a `create` rule.
2.  **Admin Roles:** Administrator privileges are handled via a dedicated top-level collection `/admins/{userId}`. Instead of an `isAdmin` boolean field within the `User` document (which would require a `get()` call to the user profile), the *existence* of a document in `/admins/{userId}` with `request.auth.uid` as its ID grants admin status. This design pattern, 'Existence over Content,' provides explicit, easily auditable, and authorization-independent role checks using `exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/admins/$(request.auth.uid))`. This prevents the need to retrieve and inspect user profiles to determine administrative rights.

**QAPs (Queries as Permissions) Support:**
1.  **User-Owned Learning Links:** By nesting `LearningLink` documents under `/users/{userId}/learningLinks/{learningLinkId}`, the structure inherently supports QAPs for private user data. Security rules can enforce that a user can only `list` documents within their own `/users/{request.auth.uid}/learningLinks` subcollection. Any attempt by a client to query `/users/otherUserId/learningLinks` will be automatically denied by rules checking `request.auth.uid == userId`, making the database structure itself the primary access filter. This prevents inefficient and insecure client-side filtering of unauthorized data returned by broad queries.
2.  **Global Tags:** The `/tags/{tagId}` collection provides a global, shared resource. `list` operations on this collection would return all available tags, assuming they are intended to be publicly readable by authenticated users (for selection/filtering purposes). This naturally aligns with QAPs, as the entire collection represents the permissible scope of data for a `list` operation on tags.

**Structural Segregation:**
*   `users`, `admins`, `tags`, and `learningLinks` each reside in logically separate collections or subcollections, ensuring that documents within each group share a homogeneous security posture. For example, all `LearningLink` documents within a user's subcollection are owned by that user, making access rules consistent. This avoids mixing data with different access requirements in the same collection (e.g., public vs. private links, or user data vs. global configuration), which would complicate security rules.

This design prioritizes explicit authorization logic, minimal rule complexity, and efficient query patterns.
